source.title: A Surprising Linear Relationship Predicts Test Performance in Deep Networks
source.authors: Q. Liao; B. Miranda; Andrzej Banburski; J. Hidary; T. Poggio

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports experiments on randomly labeled training data and argues that the claim's apparent train-test gap depends on using unnormalized cross-entropy; it also reports zero training classification error and chance test error on random labels. This refines the generalization interpretation while affirming random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: Random-label results are reported in Figures 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 16 and 17. Other cited random-label findings are background only. The paper's principal intervention—layerwise normalization—measures its effect on loss, not a separate test of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains convolutional ReLU networks with stochastic gradient methods on completely random labels and reports zero training classification error and chance test error. Its criticism concerns the interpretation of normalized cross-entropy loss, rather than any of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors emphasize that layerwise normalization reveals a tight, approximately linear relationship between training and test cross-entropy across architectures, datasets, and initializations. They explicitly retain zero training classification error and chance test error for random labels. Their claimed disagreement with the original paper concerns the interpretation of generalization through loss, not the existence of random-label fitting.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains convolutional ReLU networks on random labels and reports training and test classification errors, alongside its own layerwise-normalization experiments. Its primary question concerns the relationship between normalized training and test losses, rather than reproducing the original studies' broader random-label and unstructured-input experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies dataset, architecture, random-label initialization/pretraining and weight initialization. Random-label points are reported on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 figures; the text highlights CIFAR-10 results explicitly.

fits_no_version.finding: After layerwise weight normalization, training and test cross-entropy losses remain closely related even for random-label networks, while classification errors remain zero in training and at chance in testing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalized training cross-entropy predicts test cross-entropy across natural-label and random-label networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing label corruption during pretraining worsens subsequent test performance after training on natural labels, despite matched low natural-label training loss and zero training classification error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Corrupted-label pretraining can impair subsequent generalization on natural labels.

record.problems: The random-label claims are largely described through figures and selected textual summaries; individual random-label training and test error values, uncertainty estimates, and seed counts are not stated. The paper does not report an explicit capability check.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Figures 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, and 17 include further random-label points or related loss plots, but the supplied text does not give separate numeric results for each point or condition; representative results with explicit textual descriptions are recorded above.

untested.parts: The architecture is held fixed within experiments, but a complete matched account of training hyperparameters for natural-label and random-label runs is not supplied.
Relative convergence times for true versus random labels and slowing with increasing label corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect fitting and test-error degradation across corruption fractions when training on the corrupted labels themselves. The corruption sweeps here concern pretraining followed by training on natural labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing these regularizers.
Within-training timing of learning shared real-data patterns versus memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: Additional random-label figure conditions are already declared in rows_left_out. Figure 8 has an internal dataset inconsistency: Appendix A describes MNIST, while its caption specifies CIFAR-10. Neither the normalized-loss argument nor the corrupted-pretraining sweeps challenge the supplied claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments report random-label fitting and chance-level test classification error, but do not establish that all standard deep networks or training hyperparameters generally behave this way.
